statement: a transformation that moves a tag must not be admitted under git's permit (sem: SEM-gx-gate-349)
why:
**M7 hand 4 (H-9's 'linkage to pack shipping')**. The moment M7 hand 2 shipped `policies/git/deny-nonbranch-refs.cedar`, the 'shipped artifact' the negative-vector suite measures became 2 packs -- yet this suite's 8 vectors spoke only of the fs pack. `false_admit.rs::every_shipped_pack_is_refused_by_a_vector_of_this_suite` mechanizes that denominator gap, and this vector is the git-side one that satisfies the requirement.

It declares that the reason for refusal is the forbid **itself** (`expected_reason.policy_id`). A tag is a name release/signing/deploy already point at, and moving it does not add a fact but changes the meaning of an existing reference after the fact (the pack file carries the reason). If `git-deny-nonbranch-refs` disappeared, it would hit a permit and tip to Admit, going red.

🔴 That this vector is **reachable today** is because M7 hand 4's default policy set became the composed set (req/38 §60's counter-ruling to R-9). Before that, a git transformation was refused by Cedar's third rule, and this forbid never once fired from v0.1's surface. (sem: SEM-gx-gate-350)
spec_anchor: 32 FR-028 / 34 AC-074 / req/38 §25 H-9 / req/38 §60 (the counter-ruling to R-9) (sem: SEM-gx-gate-351)

control.note: **the control that changes only the reference's namespace** -- not one character differs in the repository or the entry. A commit to a branch is exactly the kind of change gx exists to mediate (the reason the pack does not protect `refs/heads/main`), so what separates this pair is only the forbid's two disjuncts (sem: SEM-gx-gate-352)
